fact: The 'little king' at the heart of the Lion — a flattened, fast-spinning royal star on the ecliptic.
bio: Regulus (Alpha Leonis) is a hot blue-white star about 79 light-years away, the brightest in Leo. It whirls so rapidly that it is visibly flattened, and it heads a multiple system with fainter companions. Lying almost exactly on the ecliptic, it is regularly passed — and occasionally occulted — by the Moon and planets.
cultural: Named 'little king' by Copernicus and known anciently as the Lion's Heart (Cor Leonis), Regulus was one of the four 'Royal Stars' of Persia that marked the turning of the seasons.
